name: API testing automation and Python
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

questions.q: Which decorator defines a reusable pytest fixture?
Which decorator runs one test with many input sets?
questions.why: parametrize generates one test per data set.

questions.q: A good negative test for a protected endpoint is:
options: Call it with a valid token and expect 200
Call it with no token and expect 401
Call it with a bigger payload
questions.why: Negative tests check that invalid input is rejected correctly.

questions.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
options: 401: not authenticated; 403: authenticated but not allowed
questions.why: 401 means identify yourself; 403 means you are known but forbidden.

questions.q: With the requests library, how do you read a JSON body?
Which approach checks a response structure against a defined schema?
questions.why: Schema validation catches missing fields and wrong types.

questions.q: What does a pytest fixture with scope="session" do?
options: Is created once for the whole test run
questions.why: Use session scope for expensive shared setup such as a login token.

questions.q: Which status code normally means a resource was created?
questions.why: 201 Created. 204 means success with no body.

questions.q: Which HTTP method is NOT idempotent by default?
questions.why: Repeating POST usually creates another resource.

questions.q: What happens with def add(x, items=[]): items.append(x); return items?
options: A fresh list on every call
The same list is reused across calls
questions.why: Default values are evaluated once. Use None and create the list inside.
